predictions.explanation: Federal deficits have in fact remained very large (around 6% of GDP in 2023–25, with CBO projecting similarly high deficits going forward), and interest rates on Treasuries have stayed elevated, matching the scenario the predictor described.([americanactionforum.org](https://www.americanactionforum.org/insight/highlights-of-cbos-january-2025-budget-and-economic-outlook/?utm_source=openai)) In May 2024, halfway through FY 2024, the House Budget Committee and Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget noted that net interest payments had already exceeded both national defense and Medicare spending so far that fiscal year.([budget.house.gov](https://budget.house.gov/press-release/interest-costs-surpass-national-defense-and-medicare-spending)) CBO’s 2024 outlook likewise projected full‑year 2024 net interest of about $870 billion versus $850 billion for defense, meaning interest outlays surpassed military spending on an annual basis.([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/theapothecary/2024/02/07/cbo-federal-interest-payments-now-exceed-defense-spending/?utm_source=openai)) Updated estimates for FY 2025 show net interest reaching about $970 billion, more than national defense ($917 billion) and Medicaid ($668 billion), and making interest the third‑largest federal expense behind only Social Security and Medicare.([americanactionforum.org](https://www.americanactionforum.org/insight/sizing-up-interest-payments-on-the-national-debt/?utm_source=openai)) Thus, within a few years of the podcast, and under roughly the fiscal and rate conditions he assumed, annual net interest outlays did indeed exceed at least one of Medicare/Medicaid, Social Security, or the military (in fact, multiple of them), so the core prediction is currently borne out, even though the longer‑term claim that interest will become significantly larger than those items cannot yet be fully evaluated.

predictions.explanation:
The prediction is about **the next decade** after July 19, 2025: that, if policies stay roughly the same, *net interest on the federal debt will eventually become the single largest federal budget line item*, larger than each of Social Security, Medicare/Medicaid, and defense individually.

As of **November 30, 2025**, this is a forward‑looking, conditional statement about what will happen by roughly **2035**. There is not yet data for that period, and the 10‑year window has barely begun. Current CBO and OMB projections (as of 2024–2025) do show net interest *rising very rapidly* and in some scenarios approaching or exceeding defense outlays later in the 2030s, but projections are not outcomes and remain sensitive to future policy changes and interest rates. Because the prediction’s time horizon has not elapsed, we cannot yet say whether it turned out to be correct.

Therefore, even using the latest available budget data and projections, the claim **cannot yet be verified or falsified**, so the correct status is: **too early to tell**.
predictions.grok_explanation: The prediction forecasts net interest becoming the single largest US federal budget line item (surpassing Social Security, Medicare/Medicaid, and defense) within ~10 years (~2035) under unchanged policies. The podcast was released July 19, 2025; current date is Dec 1, 2025—only ~4.5 months later, far short of the timeframe. Current data (FY2026 YTD as of Oct 2025) shows net interest at 13% of spending ($970B in FY2025), behind Medicare (22%), Social Security (19%), and defense (15%). CBO projections (e.g., [Budget Outlook 2025-2035](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/61172)) show interest growing rapidly (to ~4.1% GDP by 2035) but not surpassing SS or Medicare, which dominate mandatory spending. No sources project it as #1 by 2035. predictions.explanation:
The prediction hinged on two claims: (1) that the next major frontier models from xAI, OpenAI, and Google would be *trained* on Nvidia’s Blackwell‑generation GPUs rather than Hopper, and (2) that these models would show a large step‑function capability jump over current frontier models.

In reality, OpenAI’s successor to GPT‑4.1, GPT‑5, is reported to have been trained on Nvidia H100 and H200 (Hopper‑family) GPUs, while Blackwell GB200 systems are used for deployment/serving, not the main pre‑training run. ([marketwatch.com](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-nvidias-h20-chip-found-itself-at-the-center-of-the-u-s-china-trade-war-75c6ad37?utm_source=openai))  xAI’s post‑Grok‑3 frontier model Grok 4 (and its 4.1 update) was trained on very large clusters of Nvidia H100s (and some H200s), with public reporting describing 200k+ H100 GPUs and no evidence that Blackwell B200 was the primary pre‑training substrate. ([ainvest.com](https://www.ainvest.com/news/nvidia-breakthrough-scaling-law-origins-set-revolutionize-ai-performance-2507/?utm_source=openai))  Google’s next‑generation Gemini models (2.x and 3), meanwhile, are consistently described as being trained entirely on Google’s own TPUs (Trillium/TPUv6 and then Ironwood/TPUv7), not on Nvidia GPUs of any kind. ([blog.scuti.jp](https://blog.scuti.jp/gemini-2-0-google-latest-ai/?utm_source=openai))

On the capability side, coverage of GPT‑5 in particular has emphasized that its improvements over GPT‑4.x are meaningful but largely incremental rather than a dramatic ‘step‑function’ leap, which already undermines the second part of the claim. ([ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/d01290c9-cc92-4c1f-bd70-ac332cd40f94?utm_source=openai))  Since the hardware prediction is clearly false for all three companies (Hopper and TPUs, not Blackwell, were used for training the next frontier models), the overall prediction is best classified as **wrong**, regardless of how one interprets the subjective “step‑function” language.

predictions.explanation:
Congressional and news records show that the *Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025* (the CLARITY Act, H.R. 3633) did **not** pass the Senate or reach President Trump’s desk by the end of September 2025, nor was it signed into law in October 2025.

Key facts:

- The CLARITY Act passed the House on July 17, 2025, by a 294–134 vote. It was then sent to the Senate and on **September 18, 2025** was “received in the Senate and read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs,” where it remains. Congress.gov lists its latest action as that September 18 referral, and its status is still only **“Passed House,”** not “Passed Senate,” “To President,” or “Became Law.” ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/index.php/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633?utm_source=openai))
- A Congressional Research Service brief on the CLARITY Act, revised **September 30, 2025**, still describes it as pending legislation and does not indicate Senate passage or enactment. ([legistorm.com](https://www.legistorm.com/reports/view/crs/550097/Crypto_Legislation_An_Overview_of_H_R_3633_the_CLARITY_Act.html?utm_source=openai))
- Senate sources through October 2025 describe the crypto market-structure bill (based on or related to the CLARITY framework) as being in draft/negotiation, with significant partisan disputes and no completed committee or floor vote. For example, coverage from early and late October notes that the market-structure bill “remains in the discussion phase in the Senate” and is stalled amid gridlock, clearly implying it has not yet passed. ([axios.com](https://www.axios.com/2025/10/07/crypto-market-structure-afl-cio?utm_source=openai))
- By contrast, the **GENIUS Act** (the stablecoin bill) *did* complete the process: it passed both chambers and was signed by President Trump on **July 18, 2025**, becoming the first major federal crypto law. This is consistently documented in legislative records and press reports, underscoring that if the CLARITY Act had been similarly enacted, it would appear in the same way—which it does not. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GENIUS_Act?utm_source=openai))

David Sacks’ prediction, normalized as: *“Assuming the process proceeds without major disruption, the CLARITY Act will pass the Senate and reach President Trump’s desk by the end of September 2025, enabling a signing into law around October 2025,”* is therefore **incorrect**. The specified milestones (Senate passage by end of September and presidential signing in October) did not occur within that timeframe or by November 30, 2025, despite ongoing work on related Senate market-structure legislation.

The prediction specifies a **three‑year window starting from the GENIUS Act’s enactment**. The podcast episode is dated **19 July 2025**, and the title claims the *GENIUS Act Becomes Law* on or around that time. Three years from mid‑2025 ends in **mid‑2028**, which is well after the current date of **30 November 2025** (i.e., only a few months have elapsed).

Because the deadline for the prediction (sometime in 2028) has **not yet passed**, we cannot determine whether:

1. The world’s largest stablecoin issuer in mid‑2025 (commonly understood to be Tether/USDT, operated by Tether Holdings Limited, an offshore entity),
2. Will in fact establish an **onshore, U.S.‑regulated structure** and
3. **Comply with U.S. regulatory requirements** *within three years* of the GENIUS Act’s enactment.

There is still substantial time remaining for either outcome, so the prediction cannot be judged as right or wrong yet.

It prohibits non-permitted (non-US-regulated) issuers from US issuance, with a 3-year transition until July 18, 2028, after which US platforms cannot offer/sell non-compliant stablecoins. Tether (USDT), the largest offshore issuer mid-2025 ([Medium analysis](https://medium.com/@monolith.vc/stablecoins-in-2025-full-overview-of-the-230b-market-bab96c680c44), [Fool.com](https://www.fool.com/research/largest-stablecoins/)), announced USA₮ (USAT), a planned US-regulated stablecoin for late 2025 launch ([Tether.io Sep 12, 2025](https://tether.io/news/tether-unveils-usat-its-planned-u-s-regulated-dollar-backed-stablecoin-and-will-appoint-bo-hines-as-ceo-of-tether-usat/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/12/tether-reveals-new-stablecoin-appoints-bo-hines-to-lead-us-business-.html)). No confirmation of establishment by Dec 1, 2025. With only ~4.5 months elapsed of the 3-year period, too early to determine if Tether will fully comply within the timeframe.

predictions.explanation:
The GENIUS Act was signed into law on July 18, 2025 and establishes a federal framework for “payment stablecoin” issuers, so its actual requirements are now clear.([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GENIUS_Act?utm_source=openai))  Comparing those to Sacks’s prediction:

1. **“All the stablecoin companies will have to operate in the United States”** – The Act does *not* require every stablecoin issuer to be U.S.-based. It explicitly **forbids foreign issuers from being licensed as U.S. permitted payment stablecoin issuers**, but still allows U.S. digital asset service providers to offer some *foreign-issued* payment stablecoins if the foreign issuer is under a “comparable” non‑U.S. regime, registers for monitoring by the OCC, and holds sufficient reserves in the U.S. for U.S. customers, among other conditions.([debevoise.com](https://www.debevoise.com/insights/publications/2025/07/genius-act-progresses-in-congress-as-stablecoin))  Foreign issuers can continue operating abroad and, if they meet these conditions, can still access the U.S. market. So it is incorrect to say that *all* stablecoin companies must operate in the U.S.; the law creates a U.S.-jurisdiction gate for access to the U.S. market, not a universal U.S.-location requirement.

2. **“They’ll be subjected to quarterly audits”** – The statute and regulatory analyses describe **monthly reserve reporting with independent attestations and annual audited financial statements for large issuers**, not quarterly audits. Issuers must publish a monthly reserve report (outstanding coins and reserve composition), with prior months’ reports audited by a registered public accounting firm, and issuers over certain size thresholds must produce annually audited GAAP financials.([debevoise.com](https://www.debevoise.com/insights/publications/2025/07/genius-act-progresses-in-congress-as-stablecoin))  Commentators even note that the Act *rejects* traditional quarterly cadences in favor of monthly oversight for stablecoins.([theregreview.org](https://www.theregreview.org/2025/11/17/krause-krause-auditing-payment-stablecoins-under-the-genius-act/?utm_source=openai))  So the “quarterly audits” detail is specifically wrong.

3. **“Every stablecoin … fully reserved or backed up by a dollar in a U.S. bank account”** – The Act requires **at least 1:1 reserves in specified high‑quality, U.S.‑dollar‑denominated liquid assets** (U.S. currency and central bank reserves, FDIC‑insured bank deposits, short‑term U.S. Treasuries, Treasury repos, certain government money market funds, and tokenized versions of these).([debevoise.com](https://www.debevoise.com/insights/publications/2025/07/genius-act-progresses-in-congress-as-stablecoin))  That is broader than “a dollar in a U.S. bank account” (it explicitly includes short‑term Treasuries, repos, and government MMFs), though directionally similar. More importantly, these rules apply to **permitted U.S. payment stablecoins and qualifying foreign payment stablecoins offered in the U.S.**, not to *every* stablecoin globally or to all types of crypto tokens (algorithmic or non‑payment stablecoins are outside this core regime).([debevoise.com](https://www.debevoise.com/insights/publications/2025/07/genius-act-progresses-in-congress-as-stablecoin))  So we will not literally “know that every stablecoin that’s been issued is fully reserved”; we will only have that assurance—via required disclosures and attestations—for the regulated subset within the Act’s perimeter.

4. **Timing (“once the Act is in force and implemented”)** – The law sets **deferred and phased effective dates**: it becomes effective the earlier of 18 months after enactment or 120 days after implementing regulations, and some prohibitions (e.g., on unlicensed U.S. issuers via intermediaries) don’t fully bite until years later.([debevoise.com](https://www.debevoise.com/insights/publications/2025/07/genius-act-progresses-in-congress-as-stablecoin))  But regardless of that timing, the *content* of the eventual regime is already fixed in the statute and does not match Sacks’s description on the key points above.

Because two central elements of the prediction—universal U.S. operation for all stablecoin companies and a quarterly audit requirement—conflict with the actual text and structure of the GENIUS Act, and the claim about “every stablecoin” being backed by a dollar in a U.S. bank account overstates the law’s scope and narrows its allowed reserve types, the prediction is best classified as **wrong**, not merely incomplete or too early to judge.

predictions.grok_explanation: The GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, signed July 18, 2025) is in force and requires permitted US payment stablecoin issuers (which must be US-formed entities under federal or certified state regulation) to maintain 1:1 reserves in USD assets including demand deposits at US insured depository institutions, short-term US Treasuries, repos, and certain money market funds ([congress.gov bill text SEC. 4(a)(1)(A)](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1582/text); [L&W summary](https://www.lw.com/en/insights/the-genius-act-of-2025-stablecoin-legislation-adopted-in-the-us)). Reserves must be segregated, with geographic custody disclosed. However, it mandates **monthly** (not quarterly) public reserve reports examined by a registered public accounting firm, with CEO/CFO certification (SEC. 4(a)(1)(C), 4(a)(3); annual audits only for >$50B issuers, SEC. 4(a)(10)). Audits do not verify full backing quarterly as predicted ([White House fact sheet](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/07/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/); [CBH](https://www.cbh.com/insights/articles/genius-act-new-rules-for-stablecoin-issuers/)). Reserves exceed 'US bank accounts or Treasuries' (e.g., repos, MMFs). Foreign issuers need US reserves for US users but aren't 'regulated US-dollar stablecoin issuers' under full US jurisdiction. Prediction mismatches on audit frequency and reserve scope.

predictions.explanation:
As of November 30, 2025, there has not yet been **trillions of dollars of additional cumulative demand** for U.S. Treasuries driven by dollar‑backed stablecoins under the GENIUS Act, but the prediction was explicitly framed as occurring *“over the coming years”* after enactment, so it is too early to judge it right or wrong.

Key facts:

- The GENIUS Act was passed by Congress and signed into law in mid‑2025 (Senate passage on June 17, 2025; reporting on it being signed into law on July 18, 2025). ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/us-senate-passes-stablecoin-bill-milestone-crypto-industry-2025-06-17/?utm_source=openai))
- Following enactment, one analysis estimates that **between July and November 2025, stablecoin issuers bought about $44 billion in Treasury bills** to comply with the new 100%‑backing requirements, raising the stablecoin market cap from about $260 billion to roughly $304 billion. ([cryptowakeup.com](https://cryptowakeup.com/genius-act-stablecoin-treasury-financing-analysis/?utm_source=openai))  That’s tens of billions, not trillions, of incremental demand so far.
- Broadly, dollar‑backed stablecoins already hold on the order of **$150–200+ billion in Treasuries** as reserves, given total stablecoin market caps in the low‑hundreds of billions and reserve ratios heavily weighted to T‑bills. ([coinlive.com](https://www.coinlive.com/news/genius-act-2-trillion-in-stablecoins-to-save-us-debt?utm_source=openai))  This is material but still far below “trillions.”
- However, *official and industry projections* after GENIUS was enacted envision exactly the kind of outcome Sacks referenced: for example, U.S. Treasury and TBAC analyses, as well as bank research (Standard Chartered, Citi, etc.), project stablecoin market caps could reach **$1–3.7 trillion+ by 2028–2030**, implying **$1–2+ trillion of additional demand for short‑term U.S. government securities** if current reserve structures persist. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/1911-8074/18/11/594?utm_source=openai))  Senior officials like Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have publicly cited similar multi‑trillion‑dollar potential demand. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/1911-8074/18/11/594?utm_source=openai))

Putting this together:

- The **descriptive part** of Sacks’s statement — that *studies project* the GENIUS Act–style stablecoin regime could generate trillions in new Treasury demand — is supported by multiple government and bank analyses.
- The **forecasted outcome itself** (actual trillions of extra demand materializing) is meant to unfold over several years (often modeled out to 2028–2030). Only a few months of post‑enactment data are available, and the realized additional demand so far is in the tens of billions, while the relevant horizon is multi‑year.

Because we are still near the beginning of that horizon and the projected magnitudes have not yet had time to either materialize or clearly fail, the correct assessment today is **“inconclusive (too early)”**, not definitively right or wrong.

* **By net purchases:** For the 12‑month period June 2024–June 2025, *stablecoin issuers as a group* (primarily Tether and Circle) ranked **7th** among foreign buyers of U.S. debt, behind Cayman Islands, Belgium, the U.K., France, Canada, and Japan. This is based on changes in Treasury holdings and explicitly lists “Stablecoin Issuers” in 7th place, not 4th. ([finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/tether-now-holds-more-us-180110469.html?utm_source=openai))
* **Stablecoin issuers in aggregate:** ARK Invest and related summaries estimate that Tether and Circle together were only the **18th‑largest holders** of U.S. Treasuries as of early 2025, and that Tether alone was the **7th‑largest buyer** in 2024—not 4th. ([bee.com](https://www.bee.com/ar/51611.html?utm_source=openai))
* **Forward‑looking research and officials:** JP Morgan, the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee, and Citi discuss scenarios where stablecoin issuers *could become* the **third‑largest buyer** of T‑bills in coming years, which explicitly frames this as a **future** possibility rather than an already‑achieved status in 2025. ([ambcrypto.com](https://ambcrypto.com/russia-slams-u-s-stablecoin-plans-35-trillion-debt-at-stake/?utm_source=openai))

Because:

1. The prediction is time‑bounded to **“this year (2025)”**, and
2. We are still in 2025 with no finalized full‑year ranking of net buyers, and
3. Current best data only show stablecoin issuers (individually and collectively) well below 4th place,

the most accurate status today is **“inconclusive (too early)”**: the prediction has *not* come true so far and looks unlikely, but we cannot formally disprove it until full‑year 2025 buyer data are available.

predictions.explanation:
It’s too early to determine whether this multi‑year prediction has come true.

**1. The stated horizon (“next several years”) hasn’t elapsed.**  
The prediction was made on 19 July 2025 and explicitly framed as playing out *over the next several years*. Evaluating it by 30 November 2025—roughly four and a half months later—does not satisfy that timeframe, so the outcome cannot yet be judged.

**2. Directionally, evidence supports growing stablecoin‑driven dollarization.**  
Recent analyses show rapid growth of dollar‑pegged stablecoins used as de facto digital dollars in high‑inflation or capital‑controlled economies such as Argentina, Turkey, Nigeria, and others. In these places, people use USDT/USDC for savings, payments, remittances, and invoicing, often explicitly to escape weak local currencies.([followin.io](https://followin.io/en/feed/16968198?utm_source=openai))  Stablecoin transaction volumes globally have surged into the tens of trillions of dollars annually, and total stablecoin supply exceeds $200 billion, with usage heavily concentrated in emerging markets.([coindesk.com](https://www.coindesk.com/opinion/2025/06/04/stablecoins-are-quietly-reinforcing-u-s-national-power?utm_source=openai))  This supports the *trend* sacks described: bottom‑up, dollar‑stablecoin usage in developing countries.

**3. But current data do not yet show that a “large share” of all economic transactions has shifted.**  
Even optimistic reports emphasize that stablecoins, while important in certain niches (crypto trading, cross‑border payments, savings, some retail payments), still represent only a small fraction of total money supply and overall transaction volume in these economies. One analysis notes that despite fast growth, stablecoins are still only a few‑tenths of a percent of global money supply.([blog.wewire.com](https://blog.wewire.com/stay-wired/how-stablecoins-are-redefining-savings-in-high-inflation-economies/?utm_source=openai))  Most day‑to‑day commerce in these countries still runs through cash and traditional banking systems, so the claim that **a large share of all economic transactions** has shifted to dollar stablecoins is not yet demonstrably true or false.

Because (a) the forecast’s multi‑year window has barely begun and (b) current evidence shows strong growth but not yet the clear, economy‑wide dominance implied by “a large portion of these economies,” the only defensible judgment at this point is **inconclusive (too early)**.

The prediction is framed as a *multi‑year* structural claim (“over the coming years” community banks will *not* be put out of business or broadly wiped out by stablecoins). As of Nov. 30, 2025, only a little over four months have elapsed since the July 19, 2025 episode, so the intended time horizon has clearly not played out.

What we *can* see so far:

- Community banks remain a major part of the U.S. system and are still described in 2025 policy discussions as providing the majority of small‑business and agricultural lending, i.e., they have not been broadly wiped out or rendered insignificant in the short term.​([icba.org](https://www.icba.org/newsroom/newswatch-today/2025/10/08/icba-urges-congress-to-preserve-access-to-credit-by-extending-prohibition-on-yield-bearing-stablecoins?utm_source=openai))  
- An empirical study by Charles River Associates (commissioned by Coinbase) using 2019–2025 data finds **no material impact** of USDC stablecoin adoption on community‑bank deposits under current and near‑term adoption levels, with even aggressive scenarios implying only single‑digit percentage impacts on deposits.​([crai.com](https://www.crai.com/insights-events/publications/study-from-cra-about-impact-of-stablecoins-adoption-on-community-bank-deposits/?utm_source=openai))  
- Coinbase and other industry analyses likewise argue that, at current and projected scales, stablecoins are unlikely to meaningfully erode community‑bank funding, though they advocate for partnerships and guardrails.​([cointelegraph.com](https://cointelegraph.com/news/banks-stablecoin-concerns-overblown-ignores-reality-coinbase?utm_source=openai))  

At the same time, regulators and policy groups continue to warn that **future** large‑scale, yield‑bearing or non‑bank stablecoins could trigger major deposit outflows and consolidation that would fall hardest on community banks, underscoring that the long‑run outcome is unresolved.​([icba.org](https://www.icba.org/newsroom/news-and-articles/2025/02/27/icba-stablecoin-legislation-must-protect-role-of-community-banks?utm_source=openai)) 

Because the claim is explicitly about what will happen over the coming years and the system is still in the early phase of adaptation to the GENIUS Act and expanding stablecoin use, there has not yet been enough time to judge whether community banks will *ultimately* avoid being substantially displaced. Early evidence is consistent with the prediction, but it does not yet settle the long‑term question. Hence the result is **inconclusive (too early to tell)**.

The prediction ties the GENIUS Act and related 2025 policies to a *future* outcome: making the U.S. the “crypto capital of the world” **within the next several years**. The act was only signed into law on July 18, 2025, and is the first federal framework for payment stablecoins and digital assets in the U.S.([forbes.com](https://www.forbes.com/sites/beccabratcher/2025/07/19/trump-signs-genius-act-establishing-first-us-crypto-law-strengthening-dollar/?utm_source=openai))  The White House itself describes the GENIUS Act as paving the way for the U.S. to lead the “digital currency revolution” and explicitly frames it as part of a broader promise to make America the “crypto capital of the world.”([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/07/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/?utm_source=openai))

Legal analyses note that the GENIUS Act becomes effective the earlier of (i) 18 months after enactment or (ii) 120 days after implementing regulations are finalized, meaning much of its impact will materialize in 2026–2027 at the earliest, not by November 2025.([lw.com](https://www.lw.com/en/insights/2025/07/the-genius-act-of-2025-stablecoin-legislation-adopted-in-the-us?utm_source=openai))  Because the forecast is explicitly about what happens *over the next several years*, the relevant time window (roughly 2027–2028) has not yet elapsed.

As of late 2025, the U.S. is clearly a major crypto center—home to large exchanges, deep trading volumes, and new initiatives like the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve—but global rankings still depict a multipolar landscape rather than a single uncontested “crypto capital.” Coincub, for example, dubs the U.S. the “new ‘crypto capital’” in narrative text while ranking it only 6th in its global regulation index.([coincub.com](https://coincub.com/ranking/crypto-asset-risk-2025/?utm_source=openai))  Other assessments highlight Singapore, the UAE, London or Lisbon as leading crypto hubs based on adoption, regulatory clarity, or ecosystem metrics, with the U.S. prominent but not uniquely dominant.([coindesk.com](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2023/10/16/upbit-singapore-receives-preliminary-in-principal-nod-from-singapores-mas?utm_source=openai))

Because (1) the forecast’s multi‑year horizon has not passed and (2) the GENIUS Act’s full effects are still pending implementation, it is **too early** to determine whether the U.S. will ultimately become the undisputed “crypto capital of the world” as predicted. The correct classification at this time is therefore **inconclusive (too early)**.

What we can say so far:

* The **GENIUS Act** (a pro‑stablecoin, pro‑dollar‑dominance bill) was introduced in February 2025 with bipartisan sponsorship, including Democrat Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand alongside Republican Sens. * The House passed the GENIUS Act on July 17, 2025 by **308–122**, with **over 100 Democrats** joining Republicans in support, again underscoring broad bipartisan backing. ([gazette.com](https://gazette.com/2025/07/17/house-passes-crypto-week-legislation-after-republican-revolt-409546b4-2f9a-5714-b266-da7202783227/?utm_source=openai))

([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/07/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/?utm_source=openai))
* Additional crypto‑related bills (the **Digital Asset Market Clarity Act** and the **Anti‑CBDC Surveillance State Act**) have also advanced with some Democratic support, but they show more mixed, partly partisan voting patterns, and CLARITY is still awaiting Senate action. ([nypost.com](https://nypost.com/2025/07/17/us-news/house-passes-trio-of-crypto-bills-to-help-regulate-digital-currency-bars-fed-from-making-its-own/?utm_source=openai))

These datapoints suggest that as of late 2025 there **is** meaningful bipartisan support, including from a non‑trivial number of Democrats, for at least one major pro‑stablecoin, pro‑dollar bill. However, the prediction goes further: it asserts that such bipartisan support **will persist and likely grow over the next few years.** Whether Democratic support in the Senate continues to increase—or instead plateaus or reverses—as future crypto and stablecoin bills are debated (e.g., broader market‑structure or follow‑on legislation) cannot yet be assessed so soon after the prediction date.

Because the evaluation period (“the next few years”) has not elapsed and future legislative behavior remains uncertain, the correct status now is **inconclusive (too early)**, even though early evidence is directionally consistent with the prediction.

predictions.explanation:
Evidence shows that by well before October 2025 a follow‑on **CLARITY** market‑structure bill for non‑stablecoin digital assets had in fact been drafted and significantly advanced in the U.S. Congress:

- After the GENIUS Act established a federal framework for payment stablecoins and was signed into law on July 18, 2025, news coverage described it as the first major stablecoin law and noted that the administration and congressional leaders were already pointing to a broader crypto market‑structure bill as the next step. 【0news13】【0search15】
- The **Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025** ("CLARITY Act of 2025", H.R. 3633) was introduced on May 29, 2025. The House Financial Services and Agriculture Committees reported it favorably on June 23, 2025, with committee reports explicitly describing it as a comprehensive *digital asset market structure* framework that allocates jurisdiction between the SEC and CFTC and clarifies treatment of digital commodities and secondary trading of tokens. 【0search1】
- The bill passed the U.S. House on July 17, 2025 (294–134) and on September 18, 2025 was **received in the Senate and referred to the Senate Banking Committee**, with its official status shown as "Passed House"—all well before October 2025. 【2view0】
- Associated press coverage of the July 17 House votes explicitly distinguishes three separate crypto bills: a bipartisan **stablecoin regulation bill**, a **market structure bill defining which digital assets are commodities or securities**, and a CBDC‑ban bill, with the market‑structure bill heading to the Senate. 【0news14】 This matches the predicted idea of a follow‑on non‑stablecoin market‑structure measure.
- On July 23, 2025, the Senate Banking Committee chair announced an initial discussion draft of broader digital‑asset market‑structure legislation, explicitly framed as *building on* both the GENIUS Act and the House‑passed CLARITY Act—indicating active intent to advance such a framework in the Senate. 【0search2】

By October 2025, therefore, a CLARITY‑branded market‑structure bill for non‑stablecoin digital assets had been drafted, moved through House committees, passed the House, and been taken up in the Senate, with leadership clearly signaling an aim to pass it. That satisfies the normalized prediction that a follow‑on “Clarity” market‑structure bill for non‑stablecoin tokens would be **drafted, advanced, and positioned for passage by October 2025**, even though it had not yet become law by that date.
predictions.grok_explanation: The prediction came true. H.R. 3633, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (CLARITY Act), was introduced (drafted) in the House on May 29, 2025 ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633)). It advanced through House committees in June 2025 and passed the House on July 17, 2025 ([govtrack.us](https://www.govtrack.us/congress/bills/119/hr3633), [axios.com July 17, 2025](https://www.axios.com/2025/07/17/house-crpto-market-structure-clarity-passes)). It establishes market structure rules (e.g., CFTC regulation of digital commodity exchanges/brokers for non-stablecoin tokens) as a follow-on to the GENIUS Act for stablecoins ([congress.gov bill text](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633/text)). Efforts aimed for passage by October 2025 align with Sacks' quote and congressional 'Crypto Week' push (e.g., [financialservices.house.gov July 2025](https://financialservices.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=410793)); Senate received it Sept. 18, 2025, with Sen. Kennedy discussing quick movement on Oct. 16 ([kennedy.senate.gov](https://www.kennedy.senate.gov/public/2025/10/kennedy-on-crypto-market-structure-bill-i-hope-we-ll-move-it-quickly-but-i-hope-we-ll-move-deliberately)). As of Dec. 1, 2025, it remains in Senate Banking ([congress.gov actions](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633/all-actions)), but the prediction required only drafting, advancement, and aiming by October, all fulfilled.
